words: tron
the inference program under test; its source is the positron-ai/tron repository
PR 4424, the child

the open draft pull request "VNNI K: store the K cache of 128-dimension heads in the AMX VNNI layout, with a shared block save" (branch jhan-amx-vnniK, head 30c4ac82cb). After the new parent PR exists, PR 4424 is rebased onto it and is then called the child
the parent PR
the new pull request that issue #4525 asks for: typed access to the existing V and K caches on main, with no new layout
Ben, the reviewer
the tron maintainer who reviewed PR 4424 on 2026-09-21 (a worker-index question, a review asking for typed tensors, and an API sketch). The revised design calls him "the reviewer"
issue #4525
the GitHub issue codex created for the parent PR; jhan edited its title and first sentence on 2026-09-22 00:10 UTC; unchanged since
KV cache, K, V
the saved key (K) and value (V) vectors of earlier tokens; attention reads them
page, slot, head, D

a page holds 64 token positions; a slot is the cache region of one layer (or of several layers that share it); a head is one attention head; D is the head size, the number of values per token per head (128 for PR 4424's models)
bf16
the 16-bit brain floating-point format used for cached K and V
AMX, AVX-512, 16-lane and 8-lane builds

AMX and AVX-512 are CPU instruction sets. tron's vector width TRON_CHUNK_SIZE is 16 fp32 values with AVX-512 (the 16-lane build) and 8 without (the 8-lane build); the 8-lane build stores V row-major, so it has no pair-interleaved V
packed V (pair-interleaved V)
today's V storage in the 16-lane build: for each dimension, tokens 2p and 2p+1 sit next to each other. Element offset = (token/2)*(2*D) + 2*dim + token%2
native K
today's K storage: one token's D values consecutive in memory (row-major)
blocked packed K (VNNI K)
PR 4424's K storage for 128-dimension heads: two consecutive dimensions of one token share a 4-byte unit, and 16 tokens share one 64-byte line
expr, view, const_view, tensor

tron's expression interface (h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp), its typed pointer views over regularly laid-out memory and their read-only form (h/tron/tensor/view.hpp), and its owning arrays (h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp)
kv_block
the struct that holds K then V for one head of one slot in one page (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp)
set_v, get_v, append_v, scaled_v, v_data
today's V functions in kv_cache.hpp: write one token, read one token, copy one token between pages, compute the weighted V sum, and return the raw pointer of a V plane
save_v_impl
the model function (h/tron/models/model.hpp) that stores one token's V into the cache during a forward pass; it calls page::set_v
Zero-Initialized V Slots invariant

the rule in kv_cache.hpp that every even-token V write zeroes its odd partner row. The weighted sum reads a whole pair even when the token count is odd, and NaN times 0 is NaN, so the padding row must be zero
arena, book
an arena is one allocated memory region holding cache blocks; book is the class that owns the arenas and the pages
EAGLE
the speculative model; its cache adds one extra physical KV slot and a separate embedding buffer (x_data); it requires uniform geometry
GOF, page_info
group of four: four tokens of K and V staged for the FPGA's hardware KV cache; the staging code reaches a page's rows through the page_info callbacks in h/tron/gof.hpp (namespace tron::hardware)
CI, Nix test build, TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, TRON_K_VNNI

CI is the automated build and test. The Nix test build is the required CI lane. The two CMake options compile the AMX attention kernels and PR 4424's K layout; the Nix lane sets neither. Issue #3997 tracks the AMX gap
codex, the design, the second revision

codex is the agent jhan asked to answer Ben; the design is the page it wrote, status/design-new-tensor-type.html; the second revision is the version finalized 2026-09-22 06:24 UTC (121,774 bytes) after the round-2 review. It is the version reviewed here
round 1, F.. and C.. ids

the first Claude review of the original design (2026-09-22 ~03:00 UTC), archived as [claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1.html](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1.html). Its 58 retained findings are F01-F59 (finders) and C01-C09 (completeness critic)
round 2, N.. and M.. ids

the second Claude review, of the first revision (2026-09-22 ~06:20 UTC), archived as [claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r2.html](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r2.html). It graded the 58 round-1 findings (35 resolved, 20 partly, 3 deferred) and added 64 findings N01-N62 (finders) and M01-M08 (critic). The design cites these ids in brackets, for example [N13]
round 3, G.. and H.. ids, the 87 open items

this review. G.. are new findings from the ten finders, H.. from the completeness critic. The 87 open items are the 64 round-2 findings plus the 23 round-1 findings that round 2 graded partly or deferred; section 3 grades each against the second revision
v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view, v_vnni_row, detail::v_vnni_access

the design's names for the packed-V owner (the aligned array inside the cache block), the typed rank-2 view over it, its logical row expression, and the friend helper that alone may read the packed pointer
append_v_row, load_row, copy_token

the design's typed bulk operations: write one token's V row into the packed plane (an even token zeroes its odd partner), read one row out, copy one token between planes. The design adds no copy_plane for V
kv_cache_fwd.hpp, v_vnni.hpp, k_vnni.hpp
the design's new headers: a declarations-only header (no intrinsics) that amx_attn_iface.hpp includes, the V definitions header, and the child's K definitions header under h/tron/tensor/
native_k_view, const_native_k_view
the design's aliases for today's row-major K view and its read-only form (view / const_view with explicit strides Cols, 1); no new K storage class in the parent
k_storage, k_vnni_tensor, k_vnni_view, k_packed

the child's typed K storage as the design specifies it: a std::conditional_t that selects the packed owner for 128-dimension heads and the existing array otherwise, its view, and the accessor that replaces the raw k_vnni_plane pointer
decision record, Q1-Q4, D5
the table in design section 2: four questions for Ben with a proposed choice, a fallback if rejected, and a record status, plus D5, the native-K typing scope that jhan requested
TRON_IGNORE_NAN
a compile definition that tron sets in every non-Debug GCC/Clang build (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:293); with it, the generic bf16 conversion does not preserve NaNs whose upper mantissa bits are zero
page_supports_uniform_kv_access
a compile-time probe in t/t_llama_unit.cpp:105 that checks a page type offers the uniform K/V accessors; the design has it rewritten for the typed get_v destination
8-lane baseline limit

the design's statement that t_llama_unit and t_heterogeneous_scheduler do not compile in the 8-lane build at unmodified main (they call the 16-lane-only set_v/get_v), so the parent's 8-lane acceptance excludes them
RUN_TESTS, passage marker

in the required GCP Nix workflow, RUN_TESTS is true only when the test identity has not passed before or the run is a rerun; the passage marker records a passed identity so a later run may skip the tests
for_each_active_slot, storage_location, slot_base
book members the design reuses to enumerate physical KV slots with their compile-time geometry, to learn which arena a slot lives in, and to compute its address
checker, re-grader, finder, verifier, critic, judge

review agents of this round. A checker graded a batch of known items against the second revision; two re-graders (a source-truth lens and a fairness lens) independently re-graded each; the majority of the three decided. Ten finders looked for new defects; one merge agent removed duplicates; three verifiers tried to refute each candidate; a finding survived when at least two could not. A completeness critic added candidates that went through the same verification. Three judges gave independent implementability verdicts
resolved, partly, deferred, unresolved, regressed
disposition statuses; the table in section 3 gives the meaning of each
blocker, major, minor, note
severities; the table in section 4 gives the meaning of each
detail::scaled_v_expr, the weighted V sum

the struct in kv_cache.hpp that computes the attention-weighted sum of a page's V rows on the AVX-512 path; today it reads the packed plane through a raw pointer. G01 is about how it gets that address under the new types
t_amx_numerics PV case
the unit test case that compares the AMX PV kernel (weights times V) with the AVX path; today it hand-packs a std::vector page and passes its pointer to the kernel
lint-notes
a separate Make target that checks every 'See Note [X]' comment has a matching Note definition; the required Lint CI check runs it, make lint does not

dispo_intro: Each of the 87 open items (64 round-2 findings and 23 round-1 residuals) was checked against the second revision by one checker agent and then independently re-graded by two adversarial re-graders (a source-truth lens and a fairness lens). The status below is the majority of the three; a split vote (three different statuses) keeps the checker's status and is flagged. Where I (the lead) changed a status after reading the votes, the row says so.
method: This round used the same shape as round 2, with more finders. The lead first re-verified the facts the design relies on (comment-site line ranges, CMake and Nix flags, workflow steps, child names) against the pinned commits and refreshed the live state of main, issue #4525 and PR 4424; that record is evidence/claude-review-r3/lead-verified-facts-r3.md.

Numbers of this round: 234 agents, 28.2 million tokens, 2 hours 15 minutes; 17 disposition batches (51 agents), 10 finders, 1 merge agent, 52 merged candidates with 156 verifier votes, 1 critic with 4 candidates and 12 votes, 3 judges. The workflow result is evidence/claude-review-r3/workflow-result.json; the inner result (the script's return value) is workflow-result-inner.json.
method_bullets: Dispositions: 17 batches of 3 to 7 items; per batch one checker and two re-graders (source-truth, fairness); majority of three; batch files in evidence/claude-review-r3/batches/.

New findings: 10 finders (C++ interface, behavior and arena construction, process and CI, handoff actionability, fidelity to Ben and jhan, simplicity and scope, formulas and page quality, the child's needs, regression hunt on the round-2 to round-3 diff, section-9 honesty audit), plus new defects the checkers found in the fixes; one merge agent deduplicated; three verifiers (source, design-text fairness, intent) per candidate; a finding survived when at least two could not refute it; the lead read every vote before grading.
Completeness critic after verification; its candidates went through the same three verifiers.
Three judges (implementer, maintainer, risk) read the design and the review summary independently.

Limits: no code was compiled or run; no chromium on this host, so the page was checked structurally (ASCII, anchors, links) and not rendered; agents can make mistakes, so every finding carries its evidence and votes; the lead's own reading is not a substitute for Ben's.
Evidence: evidence/claude-review-r3/ holds the workflow result, findings.json, build_findings.py, gen_review.py, overrides.json, the design text and word diff, the facts file and the batch files.

G01.title: scaled_v_expr is not named as a permitted user of detail::v_vnni_access, and its file home was dropped
G01.lead_note: All three verifiers hold the finding and narrow it: the two rules do not contradict each other, because line 249 forbids the helper to "cache callers" and the design never says whether detail::scaled_v_expr is one. The remaining text points to option A: step 2 keeps the typed weighted-sum inputs under kv_cache.hpp [design-r3.txt:373], the v_vnni.hpp operation list has no weighted sum [:253-259, :372], and section 9 says "Type both weighted-sum constructors" [:520]. The round-2 sentence that kept scaled_v_expr in kv_cache.hpp was deleted without any finding asking for it [design-wdiff.txt @old 4447]. The verifiers graded this minor because the reading is recoverable. I keep major: all three judges name it as the one sentence that must exist before implementation starts, and the PV weighted sum runs on every decode step, so two implementers must not resolve it differently. The fix is one sentence at :273 and :373 plus naming scaled_v_expr at :249.

G02.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3. Corrections applied to the recommendation: poison has two meanings on the page (NaN in the padding tests; random values in book::fill_random at :274), so the Words row must say so; RUN_TESTS gates both the Test host and the Test FPGA jobs (gcp-nix.yml:538, :605); "GCP Nix" is the name of the required workflow, so define that, not the cloud provider; the TRON_AMX_DISPATCH row was already an optional item of round-1 F23, so that part is an F23 residual. Nine names in eight groups.

G03.title: Round-2 finding links target the live review filename; the archives now exist
G03.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3, lowered to note by the lead. The -r2 archives were created 30 minutes after codex finalized the design, so codex could not link them. This round keeps an anchor for every N.. and M.. id as a disposition row (section 3), so the 64 links still resolve, to the round-3 disposition of each finding, which links on to the archived round-2 text. For precision the next revision should repoint the 64 id links and the two page links to claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r2.html and -r2-votes.html.

G05.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3; the intent verifier lowered it to note and the lead agrees: the name replacement in the live issue is F21, which round 2 left to jhan, and the design's deferral of the public edit is acceptable. What remains is a wording gap inside the new block: the role sentence at :118 carries no link, and the block does not say what to do with the two live sentences that carry the three review links. The clause under N42 in section 3 covers it.

G06.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3. The block calls itself a replacement for the scope paragraphs and names only the reviewer links and a "checklist" as things to keep, so a literal application drops the five Scope bullets, including the required-CI bullet and the initialization-rules bullet that covers Ben's zero-initialization invariant. Corrections: the repository rule is AGENTS.md:22-27, and four of the five bullets lose content, not three.

G07.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3 (one verifier at note). The live issue has a Scope list and a PR order list and no checklist. Both sentences are the design's instructions to the assignee, outside the paste block, so they do not enter the issue. Correction to the recommendation: PR order item 3 is a placement rule with no completion state, so the closing rule should name item 2 only.

G08.title: Forward declarations of bf16, view and const_view should be spelled with the struct key
G08.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3 as an omission, not a factual error: the design says "classes" and gives no declaration text, while its own block uses the class key for the new types. All three types are structs; clang 19 under -Wall warns (-Wmismatched-tags) in every translation unit that sees both, and no -Werror is set, so this is warning noise, not a build break. Round-2 N14's corrected recommendation already spelled struct view; and struct const_view; as expr.hpp:17-22 does. Drop the sub-claim that the bf16 declaration is redundant: under the design's own include rule the header must forward-declare bf16.

G09.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3. One verifier reproduced the redeclaration error with g++ 11.4 ("redeclaration ... with different constraints"); clang 19 was not available on this host. Corrections: the block has three class forward declarations plus two alias templates, not five templates; the std::conditional_t hazard is conditional on a class-level constraint that fails for a declared geometry (the design's stated constraints hold for all of 64, 128 and 256). The codebase precedent cuts both ways: kv_cache.hpp:538-540 forward-declares scaled_v_expr with its requires-clause repeated, which works only because that header can name chunk_size.

G10.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3. Corrections: round 2 already claimed the three aliases were required; round 3 extended the claim to shape0() and valid(). The host tensor constructor is at tensor.hpp:270-275. valid() implies a null view state the design never specifies (it does not forbid a default constructor). Two K test readers at t_llama_unit.cpp:703-709 use dim and valid(), but they read the native K view, which the parent keeps.

G12.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3. Corrections: the repository rule (AGENTS.md:35-38) allows structural assertions with an identifiable consumer or failure mode rather than forbidding them; the design's named consumer never calls bf16_chunk (host tensors read rows through chunk(i), tensor.hpp:81-83), so the decltype check in the suite protects a path nothing in the parent's test plan exercises. Either option in the recommendation closes it.

G13.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3 (one at note). Corrections: round 2 already named even_part and odd_part with the words "Reuse this extraction pattern"; round 3 merged the sentences and dropped "pattern", so the text no longer hints that the two private, unused helpers are copied, not called. The better pointer is get_v(float*) (kv_cache.hpp:2416-2431), whose loop the design already moves into v_vnni.hpp as load_row.

G14.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3 (one at note); lowered to note by the lead. The both-widths rule is round-2 N01's own corrected recommendation, which the design followed. G14 offers a simplification neither round considered: guard the fakes under TRON_AMX_DISPATCH and the rule disappears. Cost of the move: every AMX-off configuration, including the required Nix lane, stops compiling any kernel definition against the typed declarations. The design may adopt or decline this in one sentence.

G15.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3. Corrections: kind is terminology inconsistency rather than factual error ("poison" can mean any sentinel); the word is new in round 3; drop "must not be read" from the replacement text, because TEST_CASE "apply and join page ranges" reads the random values back as attention inputs (t_llama_unit.cpp:2026-2041). The design's own uses at :300 and :436 mean NaN; :416 means the child's 0xa5a5 sentinel.

G16.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3 (one at note). Correction: drop the clause that h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp receives the scatter, gather and block-store bodies; round 3 no longer says where those live (that is G17). The stronger reason stands: the K tensor header defines expression types, expr.hpp includes tron/simd/auto.hpp, which includes <immintrin.h>, so the intrinsics-free interface header cannot include it and needs the K forward declarations in kv_cache_fwd.hpp.

G17.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3. Corrections: drop "which the round-2 split was meant to end"; the round-2 aim was only to avoid a tensor/kernel include cycle, and kv_cache.hpp already includes a kernel header (expr.hpp). The defect is that round 2 gave the five typed K operations a header and round 3 took it away (design-wdiff.txt @old 4908-4924), while the S10 row still ties "vector operations" to h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp. If the operations move, the three detail helpers (pair_base, pair_row_offsets, transpose_16x16_epi32) move with them; qk_group uses only the constants.

G18.title: Three cited line ranges end one to two lines off: the V-slots Note, the PV kernel comment, the S17 binary-directory link
G18.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3; lowered to note by the lead. Settled facts: the Note is kv_cache.hpp:2055-2065 (2066 is the constructor line; 2054 is public:); the weights_times_v_128x4 comment runs 224-229; the CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY set() is CMakeLists.txt:66 (the link says L67). The design copied "2055-2066" and "224-227" from the round-2 review's own C06 residual text, so the slip originated in the review; only the S17 link is new. H04 (the same L67 slip) is folded into this finding.

G19.lead_note: Holds 3 of 3. This is the loose fact inside the M04 fix, so M04 is graded partly this round. Corrections: storage_view_offset_ is also read by refresh_kv_blocks_alias (kv_cache.hpp:1222-1227), not only by the uniform accessor; layer-to-slot sharing exists one level above slot indices, so say "no two slot indices map to one physical region" rather than "no aliasing". short_version: The second revision resolved 60 of the 87 open items (64 round-2 findings plus 23 round-1 residuals). 25 are partly resolved, 2 are deferred to jhan, none is unresolved and none regressed.

This round found 52 new defects: 1 major, 27 minor, 24 notes. The major one is a single missing sentence: the design no longer says how detail::scaled_v_expr, the weighted V sum in kv_cache.hpp, obtains the packed address under the new access rule (G01). The other items an implementer would stop on are the t_amx_numerics fixture route (G22), the constraint mechanism (G09) and the D5 wording (G04).

Verdict: accept with changes. All three judges say so; two of three say the design is not yet implementable until G01 and G22 are written. After those two edits and the eleven regressions and residuals listed in section 7, another agent can implement the parent from this page.
verdict_badge: two of three judges: not yet implementable
verdict_sub: 3 of 3 judges; G01 and G22 first, then the section 7 list; see section 8
changes_outro: Two things did not change. The proposed types, the kernel signatures and the seven-step plan are the same as in round 2. And the design still names the reviewer in its Words table while the text it prepares for the issue uses a role only; that is allowed for a local page (G36).
dispo_outro: Reading the votes changed one status. The checkers graded M04 resolved; the fix sentence says for_each_active_slot "dispatches the physical slot", and G19 shows the helper visits logical slot indices, so I lowered M04 to partly. Four items carry an optional clause next to a resolved status (N13, N43, F41 and now M04's remark); the remark says what is optional, so the two columns agree.

Fourteen items were decided by a two-to-one majority; none was a three-way split. The three deferred-or-partly issue-body items (F19, F20, F21) and the N42 residual are one edit: the block in design section 2 must keep the live Scope and PR-order lists and replace the two name occurrences with a role, links unchanged.
findings_intro: Ten finders read the second revision through one lens each (C++ interface, behavior and arena construction, process and CI, handoff actionability, fidelity to Ben and jhan, simplicity and scope, formulas and page quality, the child's needs, a regression hunt over the round-2 to round-3 word diff, and a section-9 honesty audit). Their 62 candidates and 19 new defects the disposition checkers found in the fixes were merged into 52 candidates, and each was put to three verifiers who tried to refute it; a finding survived when at least two could not. A completeness critic added four candidates that went through the same verification. Two survivors were dropped by the lead (H04 duplicates G18; G52 is a positive check) and nine were regraded after reading the votes; the Lead's reading row of each finding says why. Severities are the lead's final grades.
questions_intro: Design section 2 now carries a decision record: four questions for Ben (Q1 to Q4) with a proposed choice, a fallback if rejected and a record status, plus D5, the native-K typing scope that jhan requested. The owner is the issue assignee, the record place is the parent PR description, and implementation may start on the proposed choices labelled Proposed. All three judges found the record adequate. The table gives my reading of each row against Ben's three comments (evidence/github-review.json) and jhan's request.
questions_rows: Q1. May each concrete view contain its address formula? Proposed: yes; one view per layout, separate V and K owners, no layout-policy template.
Ben's sketch sections 1 and 2 (layout as a template argument of owner and view) and his own reservation: "I'm not entirely convinced of the necessity of separate k_vnni_layout from vnni_view".

Adequate. The proposed choice follows Ben's stated doubt, and the fallback is the sketch itself, so either answer is implementable. The design also confirms jhan's reading of that reservation (design-r3.txt:71); N11 asks it to state what the reading was.
Q2. Should const matrix and row objects prevent element mutation? Proposed: yes at both ranks, following tron's rank-2 view rule.
Ben's sketch: "As with std::span, a const view object does not make its elements const. vnni_view<const bf16, Layout> does."

Adequate, and the question most likely to be answered no, because Ben stated the opposite rule in writing. The design flags the departure and gives a fallback. Keep the const contracts in one table row so a flip is one edit, and settle the row-conversion clause first (N20, G40).
Q3. May packed views expose logical rows through operator[]? Proposed: yes, returning a logical row expression with no public pointer; keep bounds-checked at().
Ben's review asked for the expr precedent ("a uniform interface based upon expr"); his sketch excluded operator[] because it suggests a contiguous row.

Adequate. The design resolves the tension between the two comments in favor of expression reads with no pointer route, and names the fallback (remove the row expressions from both families). G12 notes that the mandated bf16_chunk override serves a test-only path.
Q4. Is the smaller parent scope sufficient? Proposed: yes; expression reads and the existing typed bulk operations; slices, iterators and generic writes deferred.
Ben's review: "the usual operations that we expect of tensor types and, in particular, the row-wise load/store operations".

Adequate. The deferrals are explicit and reasoned. G39 asks to restore the one sentence that mapped append_v_row to the sketch's store_row, so Ben sees the name difference explained; the maintainer judge also asks for a sketch-name to design-name table.
D5. Who owns native-K typing? Requested scope: the issue author; reuse the existing K view type through a new alias and change the native-K kernel parameter.
jhan's request ("introduces the new abstraction on VNNI-V and native K") and the issue title; not part of Ben's sketch.

Right attribution, one wording slip: the cell says "reuse the existing view alias", but const_native_k_view is new in section 5; the view type is what exists (G04). The record is copied into the PR description, so fix the cell before implementation.
jhan's step-4 premise (the child's packed-K change becomes a local change within the new type) and the identity of "the issue author", "the assignee" and "the user".
Two notes: the premise is answered nowhere, and it holds only in part (G37, N56 residual); the three role labels for one person are never tied together (G35). Neither blocks implementation.
questions_outro: Nothing in the record misquotes Ben. The maintainer judge checked the comment ids and times against the saved JSON and found one phrase stronger than his words: "the reviewer's uniform-expression requirement" (design-r3.txt:412) where he wrote "I think the way I would approach this".
strengths: design-r3.txt:148 labels 2880c3aa9b as saved review evidence and orders a fresh fetch before branching. This matches the live state: main moved to 1400fa4481 with no change to any parent step file (facts-r3.md:38-43).
